text: Tasks can run for hours with no execution timeout, automatic retries, concurrency control, and managed queues
quote: Run them for hours, configure automatic retries, control concurrency, and manage queues. There’s no execution timeout

text: Trigger a background task programmatically from your code with an SDK call
quote: const handle = await helloWorld.trigger({ message: "Hello world!" });

text: An entire AI chat conversation runs as one long-lived task rather than per-request calls
quote: An AI chat isn't a request — it's a session. `chat.agent` runs every conversation as a single long-lived Trigger.dev task

text: Stream live run updates and data from background tasks to frontend/backend without polling
quote: Get live run updates and stream data from background tasks to your frontend or backend. No polling.

text: Configure default or per-task automatic retry behavior, including exponential backoff
quote: You can configure retrying in two ways: In your trigger.config file you can set the default retrying behavior for all tasks. On each task you can set the retrying behavior.

text: Set a concurrency limit on a task's queue to control parallel execution
quote: You can set the concurrency limit for a task by setting the `concurrencyLimit` property on the task's queue.

text: Define tasks that run on a recurring schedule using cron syntax
quote: A task that is triggered on a recurring schedule using cron syntax.

text: Deploy tasks automatically via a GitHub Actions workflow when code is pushed to main
quote: This simple GitHub action workflow will deploy your Trigger.dev tasks when new code is pushed to the `main` branch.

text: Self-host the entire platform on your own infrastructure with full control over environment and deployment
quote: Self-hosting Trigger.dev means you run and manage the platform on your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your environment, deployment process, and the URLs you expose the service on.

text: Run custom SQL-style queries against your data using a proprietary query language (TRQL)
quote: Query allows you to write custom queries against your data using TRQL (Trigger.dev Query Language), a SQL-style language based on ClickHouse SQL.

text: Official CLI supports commands for managing projects, runs, and environments
quote: New CLI commands for projects, runs, and env management; Node.js 21 deprecation warnings; and a fix for the MCP server crashing on tools/list.

text: Official MCP server gives AI assistants tools to search docs, initialize/manage projects, trigger and monitor runs, and deploy
quote: It provides a comprehensive set of tools to: Search Trigger.dev documentation, Initialize new Trigger.dev projects, List and manage your projects and organizations, Get task information and trigger task runs, Deploy projects to different en

text: Officially supported SDK/task versions follow a defined deprecation and migration policy across major versions
quote: v3 is end of life. Trigger.dev 4.5.0 is the last version we officially support for running v3 (SDK v3) tasks. If you still have v3 tasks, stay on 4.5.0 or migrate to v4

text: Trigger a task and wait synchronously until it completes, receiving the result
quote: yourTask.triggerAndWait() Triggers a task and then waits until it's complete. You get the result data to continue with.

text: Use a returned run handle to check status, cancel, or retry a triggered task
quote: You can use the handle to check the status of the task, cancel and retry it.

text: Portable 'Skills' instruction sets teach AI coding assistants how to use Trigger.dev effectively
quote: Skills are portable instruction sets that teach AI coding assistants how to use Trigger.dev effectively.

text: Multi-turn AI chat tasks are durable, surviving page refreshes, redeploys, and crashes
quote: Durable multi-turn AI chats — one Trigger.dev task per conversation, surviving refreshes, deploys, and crashes.

text: Run a local development server on your machine to execute Trigger.dev tasks for local dev/testing
quote: This runs a server on your machine that can execute Trigger.dev tasks

text: Configure separate clients to target multiple projects, environments, or preview branches from one process
quote: If a single process needs to talk to more than one Trigger.dev project, environment, or preview branch, use `new TriggerClient({...})` for each target instead of `configure()`.

text: Authenticate to the management API using a scoped environment secret key or a personal access token
quote: There are two methods of authenticating with the management API: using a named API key associated with a specific environment in a project (`secretKey`), or using a personal access token

text: Pause a run to wait for human approval before continuing execution
quote: needsApproval: true, // pauses for human approval; the run stays alive

text: Self-hosted deployment is simplified to a single supervisor process started with one docker compose command
quote: Much simpler setup. The provider and coordinator are now combined into a single supervisor. No more startup scripts, just `docker compose up`.
